build.note: Same head STATE.md recorded on 2026-08-19. Upstream has not moved. The original guard run tested 5.52.0 @ c43e9ee1e2, 14 commits earlier.

S1.note: tools/list returned ["list_article","get_article"] before the restart and [] after it, with nothing else changed. GET /admin/admin-tokens/5 after the restart shows adminPermissions: [], so the permission row is deleted rather than the ability being derived differently. The token still authenticates (tools/call answers 'Tool list_article disabled', not an auth error). No warning or log line accompanies the deletion.

S2.note: update_article with categories {set:[cat1], connect:[cat2]} answered 200 with no isError and updatedAt advanced. The get_article read-back, which the original run never reached, holds cat1 only, confirming connect was silently discarded.

S3.note: categories {set: null} answered 200 with no isError and updatedAt advanced by 71 ms, and the read-back still returns the category. Matches the sibling run 2026-08-14T15-15-28Z_32215874 on every observable.

S4.note: Three consecutive update_article replies all report "categories":[] while get_article at the identical updatedAt returns one category. Every write reply observed in the session was false.

S5.note: $null:true and $notNull:true both rejected with MCP error -32602 'Invalid input at filters.$and[1].authorName'. The $notNull half, never executed by the original run, fails identically. $null:null, which the advertised schema does accept, returned the two documents that HAVE an author name, the exact complement of what was asked, with no error.

S6.note: With a BEGIN IMMEDIATE lock held on the sqlite file from a second process, MCP create_article returned the full insert statement with every bound value plus 'database is locked'. The same failure through POST /api/articles returned a scrubbed 500 with no SQL, which localises the fix to the MCP boundary.

S7.note: list_article with no pagination arguments returned pagination {page:1,pageSize:10,pageCount:1,total:3}, while the same server's tools/list advertises pageSize 'default: 25, max: 100' and REST on the same instance answers pageSize 25.

S8.note: DELETE ?status=draft answered 500 with 'Cannot delete a draft document' logged at repository.js:273 and the document intact. The ?status=published half, inferred from source in the review and observed here for the first time, answered 204 and left both the draft and the published version 404.

S9.note: DELETE and POST on an unrouted path both answer 405 with Allow: HEAD, GET and a text/plain 'Method Not Allowed', while GET on the same path answers 404 with the documented JSON envelope. DELETE /api/articles answers 405 with a truthful Allow: HEAD, GET, POST, which supports the review's note about step 4 of the yaml.

S10.note: The bulk-unpublish alertdialog reads 'Confirmation' / 'Are you sure you want to unpublish these entries?' with buttons Cancel and Confirm and zero buttons named Unpublish. Clicking Confirm does unpublish both entries, so the defect is label-only. The bulk-publish dialog does end on a button named Publish. A guided-tour popover on a fresh admin user had to be dismissed first.

S11.note: Wider than filed. The plaintext accessKey comes back on every GET /admin/admin-tokens/:id, and the escalation the review flagged as unexercised is confirmed: an admin token whose only permission is admin::admin-tokens.read read a sibling token's full 256-character key, then served six content-manager MCP tools it had none of and created an article. Recommend re-routing as a security report.

S15.note: GET an unknown documentId answers {"status":404,"name":"NotFoundError","message":"Not Found","details":{}} where the docs print 'Document not found'. A write with the read-only token answers message 'Forbidden' where the docs promise 'Forbidden access'. An anonymous read answers the same 403 body, so the docs' Unauthorized/Forbidden split matches neither case.

S16.note: GET /api/articles/:documentId returns data keys id, documentId and the flattened attributes only. meta appears exactly once, as a sibling of data, and is {}.
